# Review, pass 1 — odyssey-110 (Odyssey 22.398–501)

Reviewer pass 1 of 2 (before `gloss.json`). `units.json` edited in place by script; `t` verified byte-identical to the draft's before and after (60 units, same order). New text was checked against the house table in `conventions.md`, the published parts at the repository root, and the shipped notes. No modern translation was opened.

## Counts

- Findings acted on: 58 (rows below; each row is one finding on one line, possibly in several fields)
- High: 2  ·  Medium: 27  ·  Low: 29
- Open (not fixable by the reviewer): 1, the English layers at 22.433–434 (see Open items). It is the same finding as the first high row.
- Fields touched: `l` in 16 units, `i` in 19 units, `n` in 31 units (script count); `t`, `p`, `v`, `ln`, `mark` untouched.

Severity: high = the text says something false or the opposite of the Greek; medium = a false grammatical label or a break with the fixed table or with shipped usage of a stock word; low = punctuation, register, claims beyond the part, over-length, tidying.

## `new-renderings.md`

Checked row by row against the house table and the shipped parts (grep over all published `odyssey-NNN.json`).

Dropped as duplicates of an existing table row (the runbook copies the rows into the table, so a conflicting duplicate would have been a second rule): ὁσίη (table 16.423: `l` holy, `i` right; the row said "right" in both and called "holy" reserved), σχέτλιος (table 9.295, same words), ἐϋσταθής (table 20.258: `l` well-standing, `i` sturdy; the row said "well-founded"), εὐερκής (table 17.267: `l` well-fenced, `i` well-secured; the row said "well-fenced" in both), τανυήκης (table 10.439: long-pointed; the row said "long-edged"), ὑπερώϊα (table 18.302 and 19.600), ἀγαπάζομαι (table 17.35).

Rewritten to agree with the table or with shipped usage:
- ἀγραύλοιο: "field-dwelling" both layers (shipped 12.251, odyssey-059; 10.410, odyssey-049).
- ἄσπετος: "boundless" both layers (table: ἄσπετα κρέα, ἄσπετον οὖδας, κλαγγὴ ἄσπετος; shipped 22.269).
- ὀλολύζω: "raise the ritual cry" both layers (shipped 4.767, odyssey-021; "in triumph" is taken by ἐπευχόμενος 22.286).
- πολύτρητος: `l` "full-of-holes", `i` "many-holed" (shipped 1.109, odyssey-002; the draft had them reversed).
- ἀολλέες: `l` "all together" (shipped everywhere); "in a throng/in throngs" recorded as shipped at odyssey-018 and -053.

Kept, with the collision recorded in the avoided column so that the next reader sees it: εὐχετάομαι (table's εὐχετόωνται "declare", 12.98, is the sense "claim"; 22.286 `l` "vaunting"), πεῖσμα (shipped "a rope" at 10.166 against "cable" elsewhere), ἀσπαίρω (shipped "gasping" of a fish, 12.251), ῥῖνες (shipped "nostrils" at 5.455), αἴνυμαι (shipped "taking" at 9.224), ἑξείης ("in order" shipped for seating), θέειον (follows table 12.417).

Checked and left alone: λύθρος, πεπαλαγμένος (table has "spatter", 13.395), νηλείτις, ἀναιδείη (table: ἀναιδής "shameless"), δουλοσύνη (table: δούλιον ἦμαρ "slavery"), ξαίνω, θόλος, ψυχή (table 21.153 "life"), αἴνα (shipped αἰνῶς `l` "terribly"), λίστρον, ἐν στείνει, κίχλη · πέλεια (shipped "dove"), στυγερὸς κοῖτος (στυγερός "hateful", table), θεειόω, ἄκος, ῥάκος (table 13.434 "rag"), νεμεσσητός (table νεμεσσάω "resentment"), ἀμφιχέομαι (shipped "poured around" 20.716), γλυκὺς ἵμερος (table ἵμερος "longing").

## Considered and refused

1. **22.433–434 English layers ("So then she spoke", "So she spoke")** — wrong here (Odysseus speaks) but identical to the published unit at odyssey-089 (18.185); the validator fails any difference, so the reviewer may not change them. Only the note was made true. See Open items.
2. **411 `i` "but hold yourself back"** (Greek καί) — an adversative rendering of καί between two imperatives, natural English, force unchanged. Left.
3. **475 `i` "for the dogs to eat raw" against `l` "raw for the dogs to share"** — δάσασθαι is "divide among themselves", and the sharing out is by eating; `i` states the point. Left.
4. **500 `l` "he knew" against `i` "he recognised"** — the note says "was recognising"; γιγνώσκω spans both. Left.
5. **468 `i` "as they hurry to enter their roost"** — the note's label (ἐσιέμεναι the infinitive of ἐσίημι) was tested and is right: -μεναι is added to the stem ἱε- (as θέ-μεναι to θε-), so the middle of ἵημι "hasten" is the form, and "hurry" is not an addition. Left.
6. **481 `i` "the cure for ills"** — flagged as a possible remembered phrase; it is rebuilt from ἄκος "remedy, cure" (LSJ) and κακά; the shipped table has no competing row. Left.
7. **401 n "εὗρεν is the unaugmented aorist"** — the glossary and odyssey-014/-049 call εὗρον "unaugmented (= ηὗρον)"; odyssey-002 says "keeps its augment". A standing inconsistency in shipped notes, not an error of this part. Left.
8. **About text "ready to cry out in triumph"** — plain-English summary, not a rendering of ὀλολύζω. Left.
9. **Marks "Odysseus speaks" at 437 and 481** — 109 has "Odysseus speaks again" for a resumed speaker, but the marks are free-form (27 "Odysseus speaks" shipped). Left.
10. **Shipped inconsistencies met and left as shipped:** odyssey-107 "well-founded" for ἐϋσταθής; odyssey-030 and -109 `i` "maidservants"; odyssey-046 "a rope" for πεῖσμα; odyssey-018/-053 "in throngs". Not this part's to change.

## Checks done with no finding

- **Quotation marks.** Eight speeches, eight “ and eight ” in `l` and in `i` (411–418, 420–429, 431–432, 437–445, 462–464, 481–484, 486–489, 491); “ and `mark` on the first unit of each, ” on the last. There is no run-in: the last unit of odyssey-109 (397) ends Telemachus's speech with ”, and this part opens with narration. 430, 490 and the other formula lines carry no mark, as shipped.
- **Structure.** Concatenated `t` equals the packet's lines; every `ln` is the line the unit starts on (mid-line starts at 400, 431, 450, 451, 456, 482, 489, 493, 500 checked); `p` is on exactly the thirteen ¶ lines (398, 411, 419, 430, 433, 437, 446, 462, 465, 474, 478, 490, 492).
- **Published repeats.** The seven units whose Greek is already shipped (416, 419, 420, 430, 433–434, 485, 490) match the published `l` and `i` exactly. In the units that only contain a published line (398 line 1, 410, 495–496, 497, 499) the published wording is reused.
- **Cross-references** in notes (402, 408, 414, 419, 427, 430, 438–439, 440–442, 442, 479, 493, 452–453) checked against the lines.
- **Scansion.** The packet reports 0 flags. The scanner was re-run on all 104 lines: no UNRESOLVED, AMBIGUOUS or NO FIT; only its informational notes (spondaic fifth foot at 403, 414, 419, 422, 440, 448, 457, 465, 480, 485, 492; correption; lengthening before initial μ at 417, 421, 489, 491; digamma at 436; ἔρχεται, ὀλολύξαι). None is an irregularity that needs a sentence in a note, so no note was added.
- **Validator-style checks run on the draft** (without building): no backtick in any note; `l` has the same number of lines as `t` in every unit; no `\n` in `i`; notes between 24 and 130 words.

## Open items

1. **Owner decision needed: 22.433–434.** `l`/`i` say "she spoke"; the speaker is Odysseus. Any fix means changing the shipped English at odyssey-089 (where "she" is right, Penelope speaking) in a way that breaks the repeated-line rule, or exempting this unit in the validator, or re-cutting the unit (which the sense-unit rule does not allow). The note now states the facts. The same lines come back at 22.496, but there only the second line is repeated and no pronoun is involved.
2. **For pass 2:** the gloss pass must use the revised `l`/`i` (field-dwelling, boundless, well-standing, long-pointed, full-of-holes) when it parses; ἐσιέμεναι (468) is parsed as a form of ἵημι with εἰσ-, not of εἶμι.
